- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.15) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.40) and price is trending up, model may overfit momentum; apply mild downward correction (–1–2%) to avoid overcorrection.
- In mean-reversion regimes (sentiment neutral or slightly bearish, price near 30-day moving average), model often holds too high; adjust downward by 1–2% if price deviates >2% from MA.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum + low sentiment, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to catch early reversal.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (0.2–0.4), model often averages out noise; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: higher sentiment → higher weight on recent price, lower → weight on 10-day MA.
